oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — inferred us-west inference pool showing kubelet restarts and NotReady nodes. Multiple pods reporting OOM/CUDA errors. Pager firing: https://pager.example/incident/1768401234 :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: summary: ~15% of infer-usw nodes in NotReady over last 7m, spike in Xid/CUDA driver errors in runtime logs, autoscaler triggered scale but pods not scheduling to healthy nodes.

Mira Patel: saw the pager. I'm jumping on this — grabbing kube status + pod list.

Robin SRE: copying outputs to thread. kubectl get nodes | egrep "infer-usw" shows several NotReady in a cluster of 120 GPUs. snippet:
```
> NAME                     STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
> infer-usw-node-7a       NotReady   <none>   142d  v1.26.5
> infer-usw-node-3f       NotReady   <none>   87d   v1.26.5
> infer-usw-node-b2       Ready      <none>   21d   v1.26.5
```

Robin SRE: pod-level: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep OOM shows many runtime pods in CrashLoopBackOff and some with exit code 137. Also seeing driver Xid logs:```
NVRM: Xid (13) GPU at 0000:81:00.0: GPC stall
kubelet: error calling GetContainerInfo: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = containerd: container not found
runtime: allocation failed: OOM on device
```

Alex G.: Xid 13 usually points to GPU driver/kernel issues or preemption. Could be node-level driver flapping. Let's confirm GPU driver version across nodes. Also check node kubelet logs for restart reason: `journalctl -u kubelet` for the NotReady nodes.

Mira Patel: running `kubectl logs -n kube-system kubelet-infer-usw -l app=kubelet --tail=200` on node-7a — paste below: ``
Mar 15 14:02:11 kubelet[2456]: E0315 14:02:11 kubelet.go:220] heartbeat missed: last heartbeat 12s ago
Mar 15 14:02:13 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
Mar 15 14:02:14 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 3129 (containerd-shim) score 1000 or sacrifice child
```

Mira Patel: kernel OOM triggered, killed containerd or shim. That explains containers disappearing and kubelet restart.

Robin SRE: likely chain: driver/kernel memory leak -> kernel OOM -> containerd killed -> kubelet process eviction -> Node NotReady. We should quarantine the affected nodes and steer traffic away while we mitigate.

Alex G.: Agreed. Immediate mitigations:
- cordon + taint affected nodes (so scheduler avoids them)
- drain the worse nodes with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` to let pods relaunch elsewhere
- temporarily increase infer pool autoscaler target for us-west to spread load across more nodes
- enable fallback routing policy to redirect new requests to eu-west or to a low-memory quantized model variant if customers can tolerate slightly different latency/quality

Mira Patel: executing cordon+taint now on node-7a, node-3f, node-9c (suspect). `kubectl cordon infer-usw-node-7a && kubectl taint nodes infer-usw-node-7a emergency=oom:NoSchedule`

Mira Patel: draining node-7a -> `kubectl drain infer-usw-node-7a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m`

deploy-bot: Deploy-check: will not start new inference pods on tainted nodes. Autoscaler will attempt to add nodes in the next 2–3 minutes.

oncall-bot: NOTE: routing-policy has a canary fallback for high-latency — use `route: fallback-region` if needed. See console: https://console.redwood-infer/routing

Jess (Customer Success): FYI, Zendesk shows increasing error rates for ACME corp (enterprise). SLA alerts for 10% error increase in their production routes. They are in US-W — probable impact. CC: @account-team.

Alex G.: proposing an emergency rule to route ACME traffic to eu-west cluster for the next 30m. Can we do instant region steering?

Mira Patel: yes — adding temporary routing rule now: `redwood route update --match customer=acme --to eu-west --ttl 1800 --reason "kubelet OOMs infer-usw"`

Mira Patel: also enabling model fallback for public routes: `redwood config set inference.fallback.model "gpt-small-quant"` (this will reduce memory pressure per pod).

Robin SRE: while that runs, I'm pulling dmesg from node-7a:```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (13): pid=3129:0 GPU at 0000:81:00.0: GPC stall
[ 12345.678902] Out of memory: Killed process 3129 (containerd-shim)
[ 12345.679000] CPU: 4 PID: 2456 Comm: kubelet Not tainted
```

Robin SRE: kernel OOM seems real. Could be memory leak inside containerd or NVIDIA driver leak under sustained workloads. Suggest we isolate to nodes running older driver or kernel and mark them for patching.

Alex G.: Action items (who/what):
- Mira: cordon/drain the 3 worst nodes (in progress) — update when drain completes
- Robin: collect full journalctl + dmesg + GPU driver versions from the quarantined nodes and open infra ticket for driver/kernel patching
- Alex: enable routing fallback and kick off autoscaler bump; prepare rollback plan for routing changes
- Jess: notify ACME CS lead and document the workaround (eu-west steering)

Mira Patel: drain node-7a completed. pods moved; pod restart rate spiked but majority scheduled on healthy nodes. node-7a still NotReady.

oncall-bot: Autoscaler: requested +4 nodes for infer-usw; expected to create in 4–6 minutes.

Robin SRE: collecting `nvidia-smi -q` from a healthy node vs affected node. Affected nodes show GPU driver 525.60 and inconsistent memory reporting. Healthy nodes 535.x.

Alex G.: that is a smoking gun. Driver mismatch between images. Affected nodes on older 525 driver — known issue with CUDA 12 workloads causing memory leak under certain kernels. We'll mark 525 drivers as impacted.

Mira Patel: patch plan: cordon remaining 525 nodes and rotate images to 535 driver. But that's heavy — we'll do safety quarantine + schedule maintenance window. For immediate relief rely on routing fallback and autoscale.

Jess (Customer Success): ACME acknowledged eu-west reroute, they accepted degraded latency as tradeoff. I told them we're doing node quarantines and will provide updates every 20m.

Robin SRE: opened infra ticket INFRA-2026-942 with logs + node list. tagging kernel/drivers and oncall.

Mira Patel: monitoring: error rate from infer-usw for top routes down from 18% -> 6% after reroute and node drains. CPU/GPU utilization on healthy nodes currently 82% and 68% respectively.

Alex G.: keep routing fallback and autoscaler for 30m, then re-evaluate. If we still see OOMs after driver rotations, we'll roll runtime image that reduces prefetch memory and enables smaller batch sizes by default.

oncall-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: cordon x3 nodes (Mira), routing rule applied (Alex), infra ticket (Robin), customer notified (Jess). Pager suppressed for 30m.

Mira Patel: handing off to afternoon oncall @Alex G. — I've documented node list and commands in INFRA ticket. If anything flares, please re-alert.

Alex G.: taking over. I'll watch autoscaler + routing for the next 60m. Will coordinate driver rotations with infra team if autoscaler can't stabilize.

Robin SRE: added per-node kernel and driver inventory to the ticket.

Jess (Customer Success): customers updated; raising a post-incident RCA request to include timeline and mitigation for driver drift.

oncall-bot: THREAD CLOSED FOR HANDOFF — last update 1768401870. Remember to file incident postmortem if customer impact >15 minutes or SLA breach. :white_check_mark:
